analysis.file_name: Oil on edge with fear of new attacks on Iran after US midterm elections - 2026-10-27.pdf
analysis.title: Oil on edge with fear of new attacks on Iran after US midterm elections
key_insights: Brent Dec-26 paused around $116.5/b on 27 Oct after a rally to a high of $117.45/b last Friday. The M1 Brent contract traded around $102/b in early October, with an intraday low of $96.55/b on 1 October.

Trump's threats of massive new attacks on Iran drove crude sharply higher in October. Since mid-September Trump has talked about 'approaching a major decision' on resuming attacks, with a 'reach a deal or destroy Iran' line repeated through October.
Reports say the US military is developing new strike plans, moving more military material toward the Persian Gulf and preparing for extensive combat activities.
SEB sees a significant risk premium in crude for the risk that the US/Israel attack Iran in the coming weeks.

Trump appears to want to delay fresh strikes until after the US midterm elections on 3 November, while Netanyahu wanted strikes before Israel's election on 27 Oct. Republicans risk losing congressional control due to high gasoline and diesel prices.
The cost of striking could be high. Prior US/Israeli strikes achieved little, and the demand that Iran hand over 440 kg of highly enriched uranium has very little chance of being met.

A strike on Iranian energy infrastructure would draw an in-kind response from Iran. That raises the risk of a longer-lasting Middle East energy supply disruption lasting until infrastructure is repaired.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan security, defense and intelligence ministers met in Tehran to discuss preventing fresh US/Israeli attacks. Oman's foreign minister said the Gulf can 'no longer rely upon the co-operation of external partners' and should seek a non-aggression pact with Iran.

Oil at sea reached 1357 mb on 25 October, up 145 mb since late August and close to the 7 Dec 2025 high of 1381 mb, when Brent traded at $62/b. SEB notes the comparison is imperfect because ships now sail longer journeys.

Rising oil at sea indicates oil is flowing out of the Middle East via Yanbu into the Red Sea, through the Strait of Hormuz and via the UAE ADCOP pipeline. October exports look to be in the range of 15-18 mb/d, though last week's flow is uncertain.

tension_points.bull_case: The US/Israel strike Iran after the 3 November midterms, with a risk of lasting energy infrastructure damage and supply disruption that pushes crude higher from $116.5/b.
tension_points.bear_case: Regional diplomacy by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan and Oman defuses the situation, and strikes have achieved little in the past, so the risk premium could fade. Rising oil at sea shows exports flowing out of the Middle East.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fresh US/Israeli strikes on Iran after the 3 November midterms would confirm the risk premium. A deal or a Gulf-Iran non-aggression pact would remove it.
